<h2>Evaluate Binary Calibration</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Estimates calibration-in-the-large and calibration slope on the logit scale
while preserving explicit statuses for non-estimable cases.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evaluate_binary_calibration(
  observed = NULL,
  predicted_probability = NULL,
  epsilon = 1e-06
)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="observed">observed</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric binary observation vector.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="predicted_probability">predicted_probability</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric predicted-probability vector aligned with 'observed'.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="epsilon">epsilon</code></td>
<td>
<p>Single numeric clipping tolerance strictly between zero and '0.5'.
Defaults to '1e-6'.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Both coefficients are undefined for one-class observations. The slope is
additionally undefined for constant predictions or complete separation.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>One-row tibble containing the calibration intercept, calibration slope,
separate estimation statuses, observation counts, prevalence, and clipping
tolerance. The intercept is estimated with predicted logits as an offset;
the slope is estimated jointly with a free intercept.
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evaluate_binary_calibration(
  observed = c(0, 1, 0, 1),
  predicted_probability = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)
)
</code></pre>
